raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With encoder disaggregation (EPD), a tokens-in multimodal request (`input_ids` plus `image_data`, no text) fails on the language server with HTTP 500 when the scheduler assembles the multimodal inputs. The `zmq_to_scheduler` and `mooncake` transfer backends and the gRPC zmq receiver all use this scheduler-side path. This affects a default EPD launch, because `--encoder-transfer-backend auto` picks `zmq_to_scheduler` for every model except Kimi-K3 with TP > 1. The scheduler stores `input_ids` as `array("q")`. A tokens-in request has no text (`None` over HTTP, `""` from the gRPC servicer), so the scheduler gives this array to the processor as the prompt. The shared base processor, which Qwen3-VL uses, reads a `list` prompt as token IDs and any other prompt as text, so the HF tokenizer gets the array as text and rejects it. #32541 added this fallback to `input_ids` without the `list()` conversion that the tokenized-input branch already has. `zmq_to_tokenizer` is not affected, because the tokenizer side already passes a list. This PR makes the scheduler side do the same.

## Modifications

- Scheduler-side EPD prompt selection converts `input_ids` to `list[int]` before it gives them to the processor.
- Text-in requests and processors that set `prefer_tokenized_input` keep the same behavior.
- A new unit test checks that a tokens-in prompt reaches the processor as a list, for `input_text=None` (HTTP) and `input_text=""` (gRPC).

## Accuracy Tests

`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, encoder-only and language-only servers on one GPU, `zmq_to_scheduler`, temperature 0:

| Request | main (`5ed306bd69`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens-in | HTTP 500 `Failed to assemble multimodal inputs: text input must be of type str ...` | HTTP 200, 1041 prompt tokens, correct image description. Same text and token count as `zmq_to_tokenizer`. |
| Text-in | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 |

The E2E run covers `zmq_to_scheduler` only. `mooncake` and the gRPC zmq receiver call the same function, but I did not run them end to end.

Unit tests: `test_encode_receiver.py` passes 9/9. Both subtests of the new test fail on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change adds one `list()` copy of `input_ids` each time the scheduler assembles a multimodal request.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -787,9 +787,12 @@ class WaitingMMRequestStatus(IntEnum):
 
 def _select_mm_processor_prompt(recv_req, mm_processor):
     """Mirror tokenizer-side prompt selection for scheduler-side EPD rebuilds."""
-    if mm_processor.prefer_tokenized_input and recv_req.input_ids is not None:
-        return list(recv_req.input_ids)
-    return recv_req.input_text or recv_req.input_ids
+    # The scheduler holds input_ids as array("q"); processors accept str or
+    # list[int], not array.
+    input_ids = None if recv_req.input_ids is None else list(recv_req.input_ids)
+    if mm_processor.prefer_tokenized_input and input_ids is not None:
+        return input_ids
+    return recv_req.input_text or input_ids
 
 
 def create_part_req_id(original_req_id: str, part_idx: int) -> str:

@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+"""Unit tests for the encode-disaggregation receiver."""
+
+import unittest
+from array import array
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.encoder.receiver import _select_mm_processor_prompt
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestSelectMMProcessorPrompt(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_tokens_in_prompt_is_list(self):
+        """A tokens-in prompt reaches the processor as list[int], not array("q");
+        HTTP sends input_text=None and the gRPC servicer sends ""."""
+        processor = SimpleNamespace(prefer_tokenized_input=False)
+        for input_text in (None, ""):
+            with self.subTest(input_text=input_text):
+                recv_req = SimpleNamespace(
+                    input_text=input_text, input_ids=array("q", [1, 2, 3])
+                )
+
+                prompt = _select_mm_processor_prompt(recv_req, processor)
+
+                self.assertIsInstance(prompt, list)
+                self.assertEqual(prompt, [1, 2, 3])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
